mcqs.question: Regarding Telangana's economic performance:

options.A: Both A and R are true & R explains A
options.B: Both true but R does not explain A

mcqs.explanation: Telangana's per capita income growth (9.6%) was lower than the national GDP growth (9.9%). While Telangana's service sector growth (11.9%) was higher than the national average (10.7%), the service sector's contribution is only one factor influencing per capita income; other sectors and overall economic performance also play a role. Therefore, R doesn't fully explain A.
mcqs.supporting_evidence: Telangana's per capita income for 2024-25... is estimated at Rs.3,79,751... Telangana's per capita income growth rate is 9.6 percent. GSDP Growth Rate is 10.1 percent and National GDP growth rate is 9.9 percent. The service sector... accounting for 66.3% of the Gross State Value Added (GSVA)... The tertiary sector growth rate is 11.9 percent as against 10.7 percent at the national level.

mcqs.reason: Telangana's service sector experienced significantly higher growth compared to the national average.

mcqs.question: Regarding Telangana's infrastructure development:

options.A: Both A and R are true & R explains A
options.B: Both true but R does not explain A

mcqs.explanation: While Telangana has extensive road networks, particularly in Rangareddy (7932.14 km) and Nalgonda (7766.92 km), and plans to deploy additional electric buses (602), the length of existing networks in specific districts doesn't explain the overall focus on road expansion. The electric bus deployment supports the focus on electric mobility, but not the expansion of the road network itself. 398 electric buses are already deployed, with plans for 602 more, totaling 1000. Therefore, R does not fully explain A.

mcqs.assertion: Telangana is focusing on expanding its road network and promoting electric mobility.
mcqs.reason: The state has the longest road networks in Rangareddy and Nalgonda districts and plans to deploy a significant number of electric buses.
